subject: Next steps: BrightGrid procurement path & marketplace preference
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightgrid.com>, Tom Bishop <tomb@brightgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: BrightGrid procurement path & marketplace preference

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion and lots of alignment on use case (service automation + customer-facing summaries). Quick recap and items we promised to follow up on: 

- Summary of ask: BrightGrid wants low-latency inference for multitenant customer prompts, predictable monthly cost, and an audit trail (retention + access logs).
- Options we discussed: hosted Redwood API (card or invoice/PO), Dedicated reserved pool, or buying via AWS Marketplace (metered or recurring SaaS subscription).

Action items / questions for your team:
1) Marketplace preference: Would BrightGrid prefer to buy through AWS Marketplace to simplify procurement, or go direct with a PO?
2) Billing details: If PO, which billing entity + tax/invoice requirements should we use?
3) Timeline: Ideal procurement target (signing + first invoice) — target date range?
4) Security docs: attaching our SOC2 summary and enterprise pricing sheet (short). Anything else procurement needs?

We attached the enterprise pricing and SOC2 summary for procurement. I’ll loop in Neha (cc’d) from our finance team if PO is required so we can coordinate invoice & SOW.

Next step proposal: if you prefer Marketplace, we can prepare a Marketplace listing proposal and share expected timelines (often faster for SaaS subscriptions). If you prefer a PO, we’ll get a draft MSA + order form ready for review and routing.

Thanks — looking forward to the procurement contact and any additional constraints.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
log an.wright@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: RWI-enterprise-pricing.pdf (summary), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightgrid.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Bishop <tomb@brightgrid.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 18:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: BrightGrid procurement path & marketplace preference

Hi Logan —

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. A few specifics from procurement / legal:

- Marketplace preference: We would prefer AWS Marketplace if pricing/poa matches our requirements because it speeds vendor onboarding and centralizes billing. That said, our procurement group still often needs a traditional PO for vendor contracts above $50k/year.
- Billing entity: Invoice needs to be issued to BrightGrid Inc., 420 Market St, Suite 1200, San Francisco, CA 94105.
- Contracting: Legal will want a standard MSA; procurement prefers a PO-backed order form where possible.
- Timeline: If we can go marketplace SaaS subscription, we can onboard in ~2 weeks after SSO/entitlements are set. If PO + MSA path, expect 3–5 weeks (routing + approval).

Attaching our internal procurement playbook (procurement-playbook.pdf) for reference.

Question for you — are there any constraints from Redwood on invoice frequency (monthly vs net30) or minimum term if we go marketplace?

Elena
Director of IT Procurement | BrightGrid
elena.ruiz@brightgrid.com

Attachments: procurement-playbook.pdf

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightgrid.com>, Tom Bishop <tomb@brightgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: BrightGrid procurement path & marketplace preference

Elena — great context, thanks. Quick answers:

- Invoice frequency / terms: We support monthly card billing, monthly invoicing (Net 30), and annual prepay via PO. For Marketplace SaaS we typically offer monthly metered billing or a recurring subscription (monthly invoice through AWS Marketplace).
- Minimum term: No hard minimum for hosted API (month-to-month), but we offer discounted committed terms for Dedicated/reserved pools. Marketplace subscriptions are typically monthly or annual depending on the contract you choose in AWS.

Next steps I propose:
1) If you want Marketplace first: we’ll draft the AWS Marketplace offer and share the listing preview (Dev will handle the technical entitlements).
2) If you want PO path: Neha (cc’d) can coordinate purchase order routing and provide the invoice remit details and sample order form.

Dev — can you confirm the checklist we need for AWS Marketplace listing (entitlements, SSO/ARNs, metering config)?

Elena — I’ll also drop a DocuSign link for a short MSA and order form so legal can review in parallel (no need to sign immediately). HubSpot link attached for the deal record.

Thanks,
Logan

On Tue, Jul 21, 2026 at 6:10 PM Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightgrid.com> wrote:
> Thanks Logan — attaching the playbook. Will follow up with procurement if there are additional questions.
> 
> Elena

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightgrid.com>, procurement@brightgrid.com
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: BrightGrid procurement path & marketplace preference

Hi Elena / BrightGrid procurement team —

Thanks for the details. I’m Neha from Redwood Finance — looping in to help with PO routing and invoice requirements. 

What I can confirm now:
- We can accept a PO to issue monthly or annual invoices (Net 30). Please send the PO to invoices@redwood.ai with the following fields: PO number, billing address, contact name, and expected start date.
- If you prefer AWS Marketplace, we’ll coordinate with Dev to enable entitlements and provide the AWS account ARN mapping. Marketplace onboarding typically shortens procurement but does require your marketplace admin to accept terms.
- Timeline expectations: if you supply a PO this week we can issue the first invoice within 7–10 business days. For AWS Marketplace we can often finalize listing + entitlements within ~5 business days once you confirm the procurement admin.

Procurement contact provided for routing: procurement@brightgrid.com (cc’d).

Let me know if you’d like a short 15-minute call to walk through the PO fields and sample order form.

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
Finance Manager | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
